formation.explanation: ApplyLog queues a future. Leader admission checks transfer and step-down, dispatch assigns index/term and stores locally before reporting self support. Ordinary follower append checks predecessor and stores before success; replication turns success into an index report. The voter-only accumulator takes a majority order statistic with a current-leader startIndex threshold. Leader consumption queues the committed prefix to the FSM; the single-entry FSM branch completes the future after Apply. Pipeline, snapshot, batching and startup variants remain gaps in this partial trace.

context.explanation: Candidate campaigns use election-local response channels, optional pre-vote and voter-targeted requests. Vote receivers check identity/eligibility, leader knowledge, term, prior vote and last-log order, then persist before granting. Candidate majority grants enter leadership. AppendEntries and higher-term election responses can end authority. New leadership allocates fresh aggregation and workers; exit stops workers, fails pending inflight operations and clears leader state. Follower timeout, persistence helpers, pre-vote, lease and transfer need full tracing.

connection.explanation: Durable log history can survive leadership loss, but the new commitment object starts with zero matches and requires an entry at or beyond its new startIndex. Workers capture the object and step-down channel for their generation. Configuration filtering changes which IDs count while retaining matches for continuing voters. Election log-order checks connect stored history to authority acquisition. Committed futures removed from inflight may still await the separate FSM worker; clearing leader state is not equivalent to cancelling all application.
